Entry 95: Dirim, Taraba State, Bali LGA, Garba Chede area, 9,000 (CAPRO 1992), Dakoid; 'Doubts persist as to whether this language is really separate from Samba Daka'; Refs: Ethnographic: Meek (1931), CAPRO (1992) only. sources.note: About Chamba Daka (Sámá mum, samb1311), not Dirim: 'Tones: Chamba has three "registers": high, medium (or mid), and low.. The representation of Chamba tone is complicated by.. "downstep"' (p. 31). Consonants, 8 vowels, vowel length described; no statement on stress or accent. p. 2: 'No modern linguistic studies of this language have been published'.
